text: 🇲🇽🎨 "On social media there are stereotypes. And the beauty stereotype turns out to be a woman who is not Mexican, or a man who is not Mexican. Is that beauty? No. It is a stereotype that they make us believe is beauty." — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum, Chiapa de Corzo, Chiapas On November 6 at CONALEP 22 in Chiapa de Corzo, Sheinbaum launched the National Day for Peace and the "ABC of Emotions": three guides, for students, for parents and for teachers, written with input from young people, to be discussed in class on Mondays in the last year of secondary school and in all high schools. She added that many video games reward violence: "if you kill more, then you are better than others." Education Secretary Mario Delgado said the students there estimated they spend about 4 hours a day on their phones, a little more than one full day a week.

🇲🇽🏭 <u>AMETEK Picks Tamaulipas: $25 Million, 650 New Jobs</u>

US precision manufacturer AMETEK will expand in Reynosa and Nuevo Laredo after weighing other states, El Economista reports: a combined $25 million investment and 650 jobs, 400 in Reynosa and 250 in Nuevo Laredo. The company already employs 2,600 people in Reynosa, serving medical, aerospace and semiconductor industries.

🇲🇽🗳️ <u>2027 Ballot Approved: PRD Out, PAZ and SOMOS In</u>

The INE's General Council approved the ballot for the June 6, 2027 federal deputies election. It carries eight emblems: PAN, PRI, PVEM, PT, MC, Morena and newcomers PAZ and SOMOS. The PRD's logo is gone after the party lost its registration in 2024. More than 100 million ballots will be printed.

🇲🇽⚖️ <u>INE Sets a Nine-Point Transparency Plan for 2026-2027</u>

With its supplier contracts under federal investigation, Mexico's electoral institute approved a nine-point work program on transparency and personal data, with deliverables, responsible units and deadlines for each action. Councillor Jorge Montaño Ventura: "It is not enough to issue a resolution. What matters is that it is carried out and that citizens can understand it."

🇲🇽🏥 <u>Deaths From Chronic Disease Are Falling in Mexico</u>

Health Secretary David Kershenobich told the Chamber of Deputies that between 2024 and 2025 deaths from heart disease fell 8.1%, diabetes 5.5% and kidney failure 3.8%. Stroke mortality dropped 6%, "the lowest level in 10 years." The Universal Health Service starts in January 2027.

🇲🇽🌎 <u>Mexico Heads for 50 Million Foreign Tourists</u>

International tourist arrivals are up 6% this year, and Tourism Secretary Josefina Rodríguez Zamora says Mexico will close 2026 above 50 million foreign visitors for the first time, up from 48 million in 2025. She added that 40% of what tourists spend in Mexico goes to food.

🇲🇽🏭 <u>Only 11.3% of Investment Announced in Mexico Is Up and Running: Deloitte</u>

Of $286.3 billion in investment announced for Mexico between January 2023 and June 2026, 11.3% is operating, 42% is under construction, and 46.6% is still on paper, El Economista reports from Deloitte's Econosignal. The main brake it names is uncertainty over Washington's USMCA review. New announcements fell 20.7% to $36.3 billion in the first half, across 55% fewer projects. Tariff threats from the north have a cost, and Mexico is paying it in factories not yet built.

🇲🇽🏖️ <u>Acapulco: Profepa and Fonatur Take Playa Hornos Back for the Public</u>

Federal environmental inspectors from Profepa, backed by Fonatur and the National Guard, cleared 117 square meters of federal beach zone at Playa Hornos. They pulled out 13 palapa-roofed umbrella structures whose occupants couldn't prove any legal right to the sand and put closure seals back on an illegal storage shed. Under the Constitution, Mexico's beaches belong to the nation.

🔥🇲🇽 <u>Anti-Corruption Prosecutors Sit on 94% of Cases</u>

Of 1,300 criminal complaints filed by Mexico's Anti-Corruption and Good Government Ministry, only 80 have reached a judge. That leaves 93.9% stuck at the FGR's anti-corruption unit, headed since 2019 by María de la Luz Mijangos, reports Miguel Badillo in Contralínea. Ten months into Ernestina Godoy's term as Attorney General, the purge of prosecutors continues. Some cases sit so long that the crimes expire.

🇲🇽💵 <u>Sheinbaum Backs Banxico's Rate Cut: "When Rates Fall, Investors Think About Investing"</u>

Sheinbaum backed the Bank of Mexico's 25-basis-point cut and said Hacienda sees no problem for the economy or the peso. She told markets to respect the central bank's autonomy: "The Bank of Mexico doesn't make decisions on the opinion of three people. It's a huge institution with analysts who review each case." Her explanation of the cut: "When interest rates go down, the investor thinks more about investing their money than keeping it stashed away."
